name: Drupal
description: An open source content management framework.
summary: Drupal permits AI-assisted contributions if a real person takes responsibility, can explain the work, thoroughly verifies generated code, ensures copyright and GPL compatibility, and discloses significant AI-generated code or text. It prohibits unreviewed AI output in issue comments, MR descriptions and forum posts, requires independently verified technical insights in AI-generated issue summaries, comments and reviews, and strongly discourages AI use by Google Summer of Code contributors.

evidence.quote: It is about making sure every contribution is something a real person stands behind.
If a reviewer asks you to explain a decision or a piece of logic, you must be able to answer. Saying "the AI wrote it" is grounds for immediately closing the contribution.
You are fully responsible for the integrity of your submission.
You must thoroughly verify all dependencies, logic, and security implications of AI-generated code before submitting.
You are solely responsible for ensuring that any AI-generated code you submit does not violate third-party copyrights and is fully compatible with the Drupal project's GPL license.

Ignorance of the code's origin is not an excuse for licensing violations, all contributions must be compatible with the GPL, including all relevant copyright regulations and restrictions in your jurisdiction.
If you use an AI tool to generate a significant portion of the code or text you are submitting, you must disclose it. You must disclose this use regardless of how thoroughly you reviewed the output.
Minor uses, such as standard single-line autocomplete suggestions or basic syntax corrections, do not require disclosure.
What is significant? Generating entire functions, classes, architectural scaffolding, or extensive documentation blocks requires disclosure.
When disclosing, please use existing issue or merge request templates if they include a designated AI disclosure section.
If no template is available, simply append a clear, human-written statement to the end of your issue summary, comment, or MR description.
It is about making sure every contribution is something a real person stands behind.
Using AI-generated issue summaries and comments can place an undue burden on maintainers. You are responsible for the words and code you post to an issue.
Do not just copy-paste the output verbatim.
Use your own words and be concise.
You are fully responsible for the integrity of your submission.

Using AI to generate issue summaries, comments, or reviews that lack independently verified technical insights (for example, using an AI tool to summarize a thread simply to gain contribution credits).
If you use an AI tool to generate a significant portion of the code or text you are submitting, you must disclose it. You must disclose this use regardless of how thoroughly you reviewed the output.
When disclosing, please use existing issue or merge request templates if they include a designated AI disclosure section.
If no template is available, simply append a clear, human-written statement to the end of your issue summary, comment, or MR description.
It is about making sure every contribution is something a real person stands behind.
You are fully responsible for the integrity of your submission.
Posting issue comments, MR descriptions, or forum posts that are not-reviewed AI output.
If you use an AI tool to generate a significant portion of the code or text you are submitting, you must disclose it. You must disclose this use regardless of how thoroughly you reviewed the output.
When disclosing, please use existing issue or merge request templates if they include a designated AI disclosure section.
If no template is available, simply append a clear, human-written statement to the end of your issue summary, comment, or MR description.
Using AI-generated issue summaries and comments can place an undue burden on maintainers. You are responsible for the words and code you post to an issue.
Do not just copy-paste the output verbatim.
Use your own words and be concise.

Using AI to generate issue summaries, comments, or reviews that lack independently verified technical insights (for example, using an AI tool to summarize a thread simply to gain contribution credits).
Most importantly, no matter whether you are using AI or not, you must be a good listener and collaborator with the project maintainer, original issue reporter, and other contributors on the issue.
Understanding an issue and collaboratively finding the right solution is a critical part of contributing.

Repeatedly posting low-effort contributions and immediately abandoning them will get your account banned. This is also known as a "drive-by contribution" where you don't follow up on feedback, or ignore previous discussion on the issue.
Dumping code into an issue without reading the thread or acknowledging previous attempts to solve the problem.
Posting a merge request (MR) where automated checks fail, and leaving it for others to fix.
Submitting code that ignores the conclusions of prior architectural discussions.
Adding AI-generated code to someone else's existing MR without their knowledge and without disclosure.
Using an AI to dump a large patch and then abandoning the issue when human feedback is requested.
Proposing a full rewrite of a module based on an AI review, without first engaging the existing maintainers.
When the full output is helpful, you can provide it as an attachment.
GSOC is meant to be a learning experience. We would strongly recommend not using AI so that you learn the foundations you need.
If GSoC contributors choose to use AI for learning or drafting assistance, they must still follow this policy on disclosure, verification, and personal responsibility for all submitted work.

quotes.quote: Contributors who repeatedly violate this policy by submitting unexplained, untested, or disruptive AI-generated code or issue comments will face consequences.

Our goal on Drupal.org is to educate first whenever possible. However, in some cases, violations may require a temporary ban so we can provide the necessary guidance and ensure it has been read and understood before restoring the account.

In other situations, when contributors show good intent and respond constructively to maintainers and the community, a temporary ban may not be necessary. In these cases, we will focus on education to help them align with community standards.
Finally, when there is clear disregard for these policies or disrespect toward maintainers or other contributors, a permanent ban may be issued.
